value: seed germination needs light (positive photoblastism): 20 to 63.5% with light across temperatures, about 1% in darkness
method: germination at constant temperatures from 15 to 35 C under a 12 h light and 12 h dark cycle, against darkness (dark dishes wrapped in aluminum film, scored under green light)

source.authors: Moura VGP, Vieira JPUS, Schedenffeldt BF, Hirata ACS, Monquero PA
source.title: Effect of temperature, light, seeding depth and mulch on germination of Commelina benghalensis and Richardia brasiliensis

quote: in the absence of light the germination was only 1% at 15-35 oC and practically zero at the other temperatures.
note: Full text on the SciELO page read through the fetch tool, which returns short quotes only. Congener of the batch species Richardia grandiflora; the abstract states the species R. brasiliensis showed high germination in the presence of light, indicating positive photoblastism. The abstract's light description (12 h light, 24 h absence) conflicts with Methods 2.1; the Methods value is used.
